reuse.why: The change reuses recurrence conversion and holiday adjustment helpers, but repeats the daily-versus-other-frequency policy across shared scheduling, server handlers, and budgeting.

duplication.why: Daily skipping versus non-daily adjustment is repeated in both date handlers, while budgeting retains two parallel adjustment blocks.

placement.why: Holiday recognition belongs appropriately in shared schedules, but occurrence adjustment policy also lives in server handlers and budget calculation.

scope.why: The edits are focused on the requested scheduling changes, their consumers, tests, types, and release notes.

maintainability.why: Maintainers must coordinate several policy implementations, separate hard-coded search limits, and an untyped config parameter despite the existing RecurConfig type.

bypasses_abstraction.where: getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange implement occurrence policy alongside shared getNextDate; createScheduleList disables getNextDate adjustment and reapplies it at two call sites.

disguised_duplication.where: The same skip-or-move decision appears as a daily-specific search in getNextDate, differently nested branches in both handlers, and a movesWeekend flag in createScheduleList.

abstraction_drift.where: getDateWithSkippedWeekend gains holidays; getNextDate gains a daily-specific branch; both handlers independently implement occurrence policy, and two budgeting call sites suppress shared adjustment and perform it locally.
